title: Make your own command
briefing: You keep writing the same deploy line for each service. Wrap it once: define
a function `deploy` that appends a line "deploying NAME" to ~/deploy.log,
then call it for api and web.
A function is a command you define yourself — name it, and its arguments
arrive as $1, $2, …  Define once, call as often as you like.
tips: Define with `name() { commands; }` — the args are $1, $2, …  e.g. `deploy() { echo "deploying $1" >> ~/deploy.log; }`.
Then just call it like any command: `deploy api` and `deploy web`.
objective: Define a function `deploy` that appends "deploying $1" to ~/deploy.log, then call it for api and web (so the log has: deploying api, then deploying web).
expert_objective: Write a deploy() function that logs "deploying $1" to ~/deploy.log; run it for api and web.
hints: A function is `name() { body; }`. Make the body append the argument: `deploy() { echo "deploying $1" >> ~/deploy.log; }`.
Call it like a command, once per service: `deploy api` then `deploy web`.
explanation: `name() { ... }` defines a function — your own command. Its arguments come in as $1, $2, … ($@ is all of them, $# the count). Define the work once and call it by name as many times as you need; it's the first step from running commands to writing real scripts.
